# Resource: stripe_event_destination_v2

A destination for Stripe's events, delivered as thin or snapshot payloads: a webhook endpoint, an Amazon EventBridge partner event source or an Azure Event Grid partner topic. `terraform destroy` deletes the destination. The destination's signing secret is not available yet. `status` is read-only: Terraform cannot enable or disable a destination yet.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_event_destination_v2" "billing" {
  name           = "billing events"
  type           = "webhook_endpoint"
  event_payload  = "thin"
  enabled_events = ["v1.billing.meter.error_report_triggered"]

  webhook_endpoint = {
    url = "https://example.com/stripe/events"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `enabled_events` - (Required) The list of event types enabled for delivery to this destination.
* `event_payload` - (Required) Whether to deliver as snapshot or thin events. Possible values: `snapshot`, `thin`. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `name` - (Required) A user-defined label for identifying the destination.
* `type` - (Required) The delivery transport. Chosen when the destination is created and cannot be changed by update. Possible values: `amazon_eventbridge`, `azure_event_grid`, `webhook_endpoint`. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `amazon_eventbridge` - (Optional) AWS account and region where Stripe creates the EventBridge partner event source. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`amazon_eventbridge`](#amazon_eventbridge) below.
* `azure_event_grid` - (Optional) Azure subscription, resource group, and region where Stripe creates the partner topic. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`azure_event_grid`](#azure_event_grid) below.
* `description` - (Optional) An optional user-defined description of the destination's purpose.
* `events_from` - (Optional) The account or organization scopes that can supply events. Use this with `enabled_events` to define the subscription. `@self`: Receive events from the account that owns the event destination. `@accounts`: Receive events emitted from other accounts you manage, including your v1 and v2 accounts. `@organization_members`: Receive events from accounts directly linked to the organization. `@organization_members/@accounts`: Receive events from all accounts connected to any platform accounts in the organization. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `metadata` - (Optional) User-defined key/value data for the destination.
* `snapshot_api_version` - (Optional) For snapshot events only, the Stripe API version used to render event objects; do not provide this for thin events. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `webhook_endpoint` - (Optional) Delivery target for the webhook endpoint. Live mode requires HTTPS; sandbox mode also supports HTTP. See [`webhook_endpoint`](#webhook_endpoint) below.

<a id="amazon_eventbridge"></a>
### `amazon_eventbridge`

The `amazon_eventbridge` attribute supports:

* `aws_account_id` - (Required) Your AWS account where Stripe creates the partner event source.
* `aws_event_source_arn` - (Read-Only) The ARN of the Stripe-created partner event source in your AWS account.
* `aws_event_source_status` - (Read-Only) The AWS-reported lifecycle state of the partner event source. Possible values: `active`, `deleted`, `pending`, `unknown`.
* `aws_region` - (Required) The AWS region where Stripe creates the partner event source.

<a id="azure_event_grid"></a>
### `azure_event_grid`

The `azure_event_grid` attribute supports:

* `azure_partner_topic_name` - (Read-Only) The name of the Stripe-created partner topic that receives events.
* `azure_partner_topic_status` - (Read-Only) The Azure-reported lifecycle state of the partner topic. Possible values: `activated`, `deleted`, `never_activated`, `unknown`.
* `azure_region` - (Required) The Azure region where Stripe creates the partner topic.
* `azure_resource_group_name` - (Required) The Azure resource group where Stripe creates the partner topic.
* `azure_subscription_id` - (Required) The Azure subscription where Stripe creates the partner topic.

<a id="webhook_endpoint"></a>
### `webhook_endpoint`

The `webhook_endpoint` attribute supports:

* `url` - (Required) The URL where Stripe sends matching events. Live mode requires HTTPS; sandbox mode also supports HTTP.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - The time when the destination was created.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `status` - Whether Stripe currently attempts delivery. Stripe attempts delivery to enabled destinations when their provider configuration is active; disabled destinations do not receive delivery attempts. Possible values: `disabled`, `enabled`.
* `status_details` - Additional lifecycle context for the destination status, when available. See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.
* `updated` - The time when the destination object was last updated.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `disabled` - Present when the destination was disabled; identifies the cause, time, and provider-side object involved when available. See [`status_details.disabled`](#status_details.disabled) below.

<a id="status_details.disabled"></a>
### `status_details.disabled`

The `status_details.disabled` attribute supports:

* `reason` - Reason event destination has been disabled. Possible values: `no_aws_event_source_exists`, `no_azure_partner_topic_exists`, `user`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a v2 event destination using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_event_destination_v2.billing
  id = "ed_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_event_destination_v2.billing
  identity = {
    id = "ed_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the v2 event destination.

Using `terraform import`, import a v2 event destination using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_event_destination_v2.billing ed_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `amazon_eventbridge.aws_region`, so an imported v2 event destination has it null: a configuration that sets it plans a replacement after the import.
